column2: immediately knowing she'd be trouble but writing the hook anyway.

column1: Kenney Dale Johnson was given a fake kick pedal to play along to during recording so he could feel like he was hitting something
column2: keeping the performance feeling live while maintaining perfect metronomic precision.

column1: The Kamoamoa Beach in Hawaii where the music video was shot was a newly-formed black sand beach created by lava flows that got covered by lava again not long after filming wrapped.
Chris Isaak sang the vocal in the tiny control room using speakers instead of headphones
column2: and the sound of the cymbals bleeding through the monitors into the vocal mic every time he enters creates an accidental layer in the final mix.

column1: The background singers were friends of Chris rather than professional session singers and had pitch problems
column2: so they were kept so soft in the mix they sound like barely-audible whispers.

column1: The guitarist James Calvin Wilsey had a custom MIDI setup on his Fender Stratocaster that let him trigger synthesised string pads underneath his own playing.
The almost subliminal background phrase 'It's only gonna break your heart' was sampled and manually repositioned in time using a sampler
column2: so it floats in and out of sync with the main vocal.

column1: Chris played two different acoustic guitars on the track: one standard and one in a Nashville-style high-strung tuning that he'd picked up from Night Ranger's Jeff Watson.
The distinctive lead guitar line was written and performed live during initial sessions but the final studio version was painstakingly reassembled and refined piece by piece over a couple of weeks.
The song had been kicking around the studio for several years with many different arrangements and band versions before they figured out what the definitive take should sound like.
The song was released in July 1989 to virtually no attention until David Lynch featured it in Wild at Heart in 1990.

column2: an Atlanta radio station music director who was obsessed with David Lynch films
column3: discovered it in Wild at Heart and added it to his playlist
column4: which turned it into a sleeper hit 18 months after the album was released.

column1: David Lynch directed a completely different music video for the song
column2: using scenes from Wild at Heart with Laura Dern and Nicolas Cage interspersed with black-and-white live footage of Isaak and his band.

column1: The more famous Herb Ritts video with model Helena Christensen was shot in black and white on a volcanic black sand beach in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
column2: featuring them rolling and frolicking on the new sand.

column1: Herb Ritts' video won MTV Video Music Awards for Best Male Video and Best Cinematography
column2: while Lynch's version won Best Video From a Film.

column1: The song became a Top 10 hit in the US but took nearly a year and a half after the album release to chart
